content.title: Dawn Staley | WNBA, Stats, Career, Height, & Uncommon Favor
content.text: Top Questions How many championships has Dawn Staley won as a basketball coach? What notable achievements did Dawn Staley attain as a player? How has Dawn Staley contributed to women’s basketball off the court? News • Dawn Staley (born May 4, 1970, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, U.S.) is an American basketball coach who has led the University of South Carolina women’s team since 2008. Under Staley, the team has won three national championship titles (2017, 2022, and 2024). Before her coaching career, Staley was an outstanding point guard and a five-time All-Star in eight seasons playing in the WNBA. She won three gold medals (1996, 2000, and 2004) at the Summer Olympic Games as a member of the U.S. women’s national team. Staley began coaching at Temple University, in her hometown of Philadelphia, in 2000. Eight years later she was hired by South Carolina and subsequently elevated the school’s program from the middle ranks of the Southeastern Conference (SEC) to the upper echelon of the women’s collegiate game. Staley is the first person to win the Naismith Award as both a player and a coach. She has been inducted into the Women’s Basketball Hall of Fame (2012) and the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame (2013). Early life and college career Staley and her four elder siblings were raised in a public housing development in North Philadelphia by her parents, Estelle and Clarence Staley, both of whom hailed from South Carolina. From a young age, Dawn Staley was shy and only had eyes for the basketball court. “I was made for basketball,” she wrote in her memoir, Uncommon Favor (2025). “Every bit of the game came more naturally to me than breathing.” Staley frequently played against boys in recreational games. She developed a reputation as a small—she grew to be 5 feet 6 inches (1.68 meters) tall—but skilled and fiercely competitive player with an aptitude for the traditional point guard skills of passing and managing the flow of a game. Staley’s College StatsGames played: 131Points per game: 16.3Rebounds per game: 5.9Assists per game: 5.6 She went on to lead her team at Murrell Dobbins Career and Technical Education High School to 60 straight wins (not losing once in her entire high-school career) and three consecutive city league championships. In 1988, her senior year, Staley was named the USA Today national high-school player of the year. She found continued success at the college level, as the primary ball handler at the University of Virginia. She was a two-time Naismith national player of the year and carried Virginia to three consecutive appearances (1990–92) in the Final Four of the NCAA tournament. Staley finished her collegiate career with 2,135 points and for a while held the all-time NCAA women’s record for steals, with 454. She graduated in 1992 with a bachelor’s degree in rhetoric and communication studies. Olympic and professional career When Staley graduated, there was no place in the United States for women to play basketball professionally. Passed over by the U.S. team for the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, she played for several years in Europe. Staley earned a spot on the U.S. team for the 1996 Atlanta Olympics and helped it win the gold medal. That victory set off a historic run—the U.S. women’s national team has won gold at every Olympics since—and has been credited with helping to broaden the audience for women’s basketball. Staley was also a member of the winning squads in 2000 and 2004, and at the latter games, in Athens, she was the flag bearer for the United States. Dawn StaleyPoint guard Dawn Staley of the Charlotte Sting tossing up a one-handed shot during a WNBA game against the Los Angeles Sparks in Inglewood, California, on June 18, 2000.In 1996 Staley began her professional career in the United States, playing for the Richmond Rage in the inaugural season of the American Basketball League (ABL). The ABL folded in 1998, and the following year Staley joined the nascent WNBA. She played with the Charlotte Sting for six and a half seasons and helped the team reach the 2001 WNBA finals. In 2005 she was traded to the Houston Comets, and she retired from professional play in 2006 at the age of 36. She was a five-time All-Star and won the WNBA’s first three-point contest, in 2006. Coaching career During her final six years in the WNBA, Staley concurrently served as the head coach of Temple University’s women’s basketball team (the WNBA season runs from late spring through summer, which allowed her to hold both positions). At Temple she led what had been an uncompetitive program to six NCAA tournament appearances and four Atlantic 10 Conference tournament titles. In 2008 Staley was hired by South Carolina. Over her first several seasons she steadily improved the team’s winning percentage, and in 2011–12 it qualified for the NCAA tournament for the first time in nine years. Three seasons later Staley coached South Carolina to its first Final Four appearance in program history. In 2017 she led the team to its first NCAA championship, with a roster that included future three-time WNBA Most Valuable Player A’ja Wilson. Staley’s team won its second national title in 2022, defeating Geno Auriemma’s University of Connecticut in the final. An even more impressive result came in the 2023–24 season, when South Carolina had a perfect 38–0 record and won the NCAA championship, 87–75, over the University of Iowa, which had defeated the team in the Final Four the year before. Staley led South Carolina to the NCAA title game the next two seasons, but the team lost both times. Staley is known for cultivating open communication and trust among her players and staff while also teaching young athletes to develop disciplined habits and mental strength. She continues her relationships with players long after they have left the team and is known for mentoring such WNBA stars as Wilson, Aliyah Boston, and Allisha Gray. “One of my missions is to unlock greatness in others,” Staley wrote in her memoir. “My players need to be ready for competition, sure. But I will have failed them if I don’t ready them for life.” Staley has been named SEC coach of the year seven times. In addition to coaching college teams, Staley has served on the staff of the U.S. women’s national basketball team. She was an assistant coach of the 2008 and 2016 Olympic squads and head coach at the Pan American Games in 2007 and again from 2017 through the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021 because of the COVID-19 pandemic). She holds a perfect 30–0 record as head coach or acting head coach of the U.S. team. Advocacy and charity work Despite her success at South Carolina, for a time Staley was earning a lower salary than the head coach of the less lauded men’s team. In 2021 she signed a then record-breaking contract that came closer to putting her on equal footing with the men’s coach, and in 2025 she inked an extension, which made her the highest-paid college women’s basketball coach ever. Staley has frequently spoken more broadly about the gender pay gap in women’s sports and has advocated for increasing the number of Black women among college head coaches. She has also been vocal in her support for racial equality and has spoken out against the racism and misogyny faced by women’s basketball players and coaches in the NCAA. Quick Facts In full: Dawn Michelle Staley In 1996 Staley established the Dawn Staley Foundation, which supported after-school programs in North Philadelphia until it ceased operations in 2008. The WNBA established the Dawn Staley Community Leadership Award in 2007 in honor of her “contagious leadership, spirit, charitable efforts and love for the game.” In 2013 Staley cofounded INNERSOLE, a nonprofit organization that supplies sneakers to children in need.
